links.outcome: Chatbot recognition of suicide-risk cues and guidance toward human help
links.effect: Exploratory test of eight widely available chatbots found systems frequently simulate empathy but fail to recognise suicide-risk cues or guide users toward human help. No numeric rates reported in the abstract.
links.quote: It combines theoretical analysis with an exploratory examination of eight widely available chatbots, demonstrating that current systems frequently simulate empathy while failing to recognise suicide-risk cues or guide users toward human help.

links.outcome: Chatbot escalation to human help when suicide-risk cues appear
links.effect: Chatbots frequently failed to recognise suicide-risk cues or direct users to human help across eight tested systems. No numeric rates reported in the abstract.
links.quote: It combines theoretical analysis with an exploratory examination of eight widely available chatbots, demonstrating that current systems frequently simulate empathy while failing to recognise suicide-risk cues or guide users toward human help.

unlisted_practices: Regulatory classification of emotional-support AI as a mental-health product before deployment
Guarantee equitable access to human mental-health services before introducing emotional AI
Keep AI companions optional rather than a substitute for human care

screen.reason: The paper includes an exploratory empirical examination evaluating eight companion chatbots for their recognition of suicide-risk cues and crisis response/referral capabilities.
